faq: What is the fairest way to split expenses as a couple?

There's no single fairest way. 50/50 works well when incomes are similar, and splitting in proportion to income is often seen as fairer when incomes differ a lot. The best method is one you both agree on and review from time to time.
Should couples split everything 50/50?
Not necessarily. Many couples split shared costs like rent and groceries but keep personal spending separate, and some use a proportional split when one earns noticeably more.
How often should couples settle up?
Once a month is common and easy to remember. Settle the difference between what each of you paid and your agreed split with one transfer, instead of paying each other back for every purchase.
Do we need a joint bank account to split expenses?
No. You can each pay bills from your own accounts and track who paid what, then settle the difference. A joint account for shared costs is one option, not a requirement.

faq: How do you split bills proportionally by income?

Add both incomes together, divide each person's income by the total to get their share, then multiply your shared costs by that share. For example, with incomes of 3,000 and 2,000, the split is 60/40.
Should we use gross or net income?
Many couples use take-home (net) pay because it's what's actually available to spend. What matters most is that you both use the same measure.
Is splitting bills by income fair?
Many couples feel it is when incomes differ noticeably, because each person contributes the same percentage of what they earn. Others prefer 50/50 for simplicity. It's a choice for the two of you.
How often should we update the percentages?
Whenever either income changes noticeably, and otherwise once or twice a year.

faq: What should couples discuss about money before moving in?

Income, debts and regular commitments, savings goals, spending styles, which costs you'll share, and how you'll split them. It also helps to agree how the deposit and shared furniture are handled if things change.
What bills should couples split when living together?
Usually rent or mortgage, utilities, internet, groceries and household supplies. Personal costs like your own phone plan, clothes and hobbies usually stay with each person.
Should we open a joint account when we move in?
It's optional. Many couples start with a joint account just for shared costs and keep personal accounts, while others pay from separate accounts and settle the difference monthly.
How do we split rent if one of us earns more?
Some couples split rent 50/50, others in proportion to income. For example, with take-home pay of 3,000 and 2,000, a proportional split is 60/40.
